newsitem.title: GERMANY: German compound feed output seen steady in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German compound feed output seen steady in 1997.

text.p: German compound feed production will likely remain steady in 1997 after a 2.4 percent increase in 1996, industry officials told a news conferencence on Thursday.

"We expect similar figures as possible declines in beef will be offset by gains in pig and poultry feed and because of promising meat and dairy export prospects," said Manfred Schraeder, president of feeds industry association FFMI.
Compound feed output in 1996 totalled 19.33 million tonnes compared with 18.88 million in 1995.
This was broadly in line with livestock producers' compound feed use.

Schraeder said per capita beef consumption had fallen by 10 percent in 1996 because of the mad cow disease crisis, but pork and poultry consumption had risen by 0.4 percent and four percent respectively.
Feed sales to the pork industry could have been higher but producers were still losing market share because of imports of live pigs from other European countries.
Cattle feed rations were mostly aimed at the dairy sector, with milk output unaffected by the mad cow crisis, Schraeder added.
Feeding intensity per animal had increased in this sector, underpinned by a combination of rising export demand for dairy products and a fall in the size of dairy herds.
Of the 19.33 million tonne output total, western Germany accounted for 15.94 million tonnes, 1.8 percent more than in 1995.
Eastern Germany produced 4.4 percent more mixed feed than a year earlier at 3.39 million tonnes.
